\begin{abstract}
For the six plaquettes incident on a link in a four-dimensional hypercubic
lattice, their complementary parallel transports---the staples---belong to a
common gauge-covariant transport space but are not independent variables.  We
define their Fr\'echet dispersion and prove that it is exactly the minimum,
over the central link, of the local geodesic-quadratic plaquette energy.  For
staples contained in a geodesic ball of radius $r<\pi/2$ in
$\SU\simeq S^3$, pairwise dispersion and Fr\'echet variance differ by at most
the sharp differential factor $(\sin r/r)^2$.

We then quantify two linearized finite-block effects exactly.  On the open
side-two four-cube, the centered six-staple curvature under the quotient
Gaussian gauge field has scalar covariance spectrum
\[
  0,\quad \frac{239}{630},\frac{239}{630},\quad
  \frac{33}{70},\frac{33}{70},\frac{33}{70}.
\]
Consequently its squared dispersion is an explicit weighted sum of five
independent $\chi^2_3$ variables.  Conversely, any link-field variation that
realizes a prescribed centered change of one interior staple star necessarily
creates external curvature.  The minimum external-curvature quadratic form
has generalized spectrum
\[
  \frac{37}{33},\frac{37}{33},\frac{37}{33},\quad
  \frac{391}{239},\frac{391}{239}.
\]
Thus the ideal operation ``contract this staple star and change nothing
else'' has no nonzero lift to link variables on this block.  All spectra are
certified by rational projection and Karush--Kuhn--Tucker identities for each
of the eight interior links.  The results are finite-volume and linearized;
they do not establish a nonlinear measure comparison, a continuum theory, or
a Yang--Mills mass gap.
\end{abstract}
